assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only peach-girl:tojigamori-kazuya@manga#second-pass-character-monograph (PEACH_GIRL_TOJI_MONOGRAPH.md, version 1.1, active_provisional) and peach-girl:tojigamori-kazuya@manga#time-indexed-literary-dossier (PEACH_GIRL_TOJI_TIME_INDEXED_RECONSTRUCTION_DOSSIER.md, version 0.1, active_provisional) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the original Japanese 新装版 manga V01-V18. The Peach Girl current-state and corpus map was read for method, authority order and scope only. The volume readings, the four longitudinal ledgers, the second-pass audit, reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments, the G4 rules, cases, results and runner, and the other characters' monographs and dossiers are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The project's BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL, PASS_SCOPED and BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime, live-action, sequel or related-manga material is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Twelve dossier states from T01 (through V01 i0119) to T12 (through V18 i0146), each bounded by an image cutoff, several spanning more than one volume (T06 V07-V09 i0146, T07 V10-V12 i0033, T10 V15-V16 i0153, T11 V17-V18 i0136), together with the monograph's V01-V18 developmental account. No default state is designated, so a cutoff must be named. Anything after his V18 i0143-i0146 release of Momo, including private coping, apology, accountability, future contact and long-term reliability, is expressly unestablished, and no in-world calendar dates are fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph states a governing reading (sincerity is an inadequate final explanation: early trust depends on intermediaries, later concrete care coexists with protective concealment that becomes physical constraint under fear of losing Momo Adachi) and keeps both the developmental reading and the counterreading alive at the end. The dossier marks goals as avowed or inferred per state (T02 jealousy he later owns and a catastrophic fear she hates him; T06 avowed protection of Adachi with inferred secrecy and control). B is not supported: T07 says the evidence does not determine the ranking of his priorities, and the motive of the V12 proposal stays partly open.

The dossier gives twelve states T01-T12 with image cutoffs, a Known paragraph, priorities, conduct and frontier limits (T03: he does not receive the cosmetic-removal scene or Momo's missed announcement; T09: no shown receipt of Kairi Okayasu's illness or later emergency; T11: no knowledge that Sae Kashiwagi authored the farewell message). The monograph orders the development from V02 owned jealousy and apology, V03-V04 staged restoration, V05-V06 search and no-fault care, V07-V08 concealment, V14 own-fault apology, V15-V17 renewed relation, to the V18 hotel restraint, stop and release. A is not supported: the dossier is version 0.1, several states span multiple volumes, the ten vectors are unexecuted, and both artifacts come from the same second-pass authorship.

Located written forms are tied to recipient and pressure: うす as an early school greeting, public オレのだから, 別れよう (V02), こうするしか安達を守る方法を思いつかなかった given to Misao rather than Momo (V08 i0041-i0044), the conditional 本気でオレとやり直そうか (V14), and 安達, オレ and 岡安 with 自分の気持ちを一番に考えていいんだよ (V17 i0161-i0164). The monograph treats 安達 as a direct-address diagnostic, not proof of coldness, and warns against inferring traits from every オレ or silence. C is not supported: there is no register inventory, conversational model or acoustic delivery; E is rejected because recipient-specific forms are analyzed across volumes.

The monograph devotes a section to ordinary life and calls it a baseline against which crises are assessed: middle-school knowledge of Momo's swimming, café curiosity about her food and childhood (V01), studying, movies, arcade visits, fireworks and the haircut (V04), V13 research and exam performance with concern for Sae's retakes, shop work in V14-V15 (offering to withdraw, less convenient shifts, sweeping), and V18 waiting, buying drinks and study and holiday plans. B is not supported: family conflict, adult career and post-ending life are thin or absent, and no routine model is given; D is rejected because the baseline is explicitly argued, not merely listed.

The monograph's scope section and the dossier's overlay state that the Momo-directed evidence does not transfer unchanged: Momo (recognition, negotiated intimacy, hearing failures, rescue, concealment, accommodation, coercion and release), Kairi (inquiry, wall threat, collaboration, grievance punch, refusal of transferable-property language at V17 i0090), Sae (credulity, refused contact, unwanted monitoring, investigation, continued care) and Misao (a specific confidante who receives a reason denied to Momo). B is not supported: no matched-recipient decision rule is given and family is absent.

Interior claims rest mostly on Tōji's avowals: jealousy and impulsive action he names in V02, fear of losing Momo preceding Sae's interventions, shame delaying approach in V03, the avowed inability to think of another way in V08, admitted insecurity in V16. The dossier warns that Momo's captions are not his knowledge and that an avowed motive need not be complete. C is not supported because few private-caption anchors are located for him and the V12 proposal's motive is left open; E is rejected because located avowals across volumes are analyzed.

Located conflict conduct is differentiated by occasion: the private wall punch and threat to Kairi (V01), painful pulling and attempted contact before Momo's refusal (V01-V02), the table strike, joining the mirrored punishment of Sae (V06), performed cruelty and object destruction under blackmail (V07-V08), the dictionary grievance punch versus the entry punch during forced filming (V12-V13), and at V18 i0123-i0132 blocking the door, pinning Momo's wrists and escalating intimacy without depicted assent, followed by a real stop and release. B is not supported: the dossier states no global 'respects stops' or 'always controls' rule fits.

Tōji states several decision frames: remaining with someone need not mean forgiving everything (V12 i0030-i0033), the V14 apology accepting his own fault, the V17 release of Momo from giving him priority out of guilt, and the V18 question whether her unhappiness would help Kairi. The monograph shows him understanding a principle in one conversation and failing it in another under pressure. C is not supported: no deliberation procedure is given and his stated principles do not predict his conduct under threatened loss; E is rejected because first-person ethical frames are located.

The evidence mentions teasing about the haircut, embarrassment at repeated declarations and laughter during the V02 repair without describing a humor or play repertoire. This gap says nothing about Tōji's actual humor.

Both artifacts cover V01-V18 with image-coordinate routes (PG-JP-NE-VNN-W01/iNNNN) and route provenance to an all-18 source-first inspection of 3,198 images by four readers and an ordered reconciliation. The dossier states that its compiler directly read only V15-V18, with V01-V14 as attributed team evidence, and the coverage note says family, adult career and post-ending recovery are thin or absent. The evaluator could not recheck the receipts, ledgers or readings, which are outside the set, and owner acceptance is pending. B is not supported.

Affirmative limits and corrections are located: the V18 hotel restraint stated as counterevidence any 'Tōji respects a stop' rule must face, the earlier strong V15 sexual-night inference corrected by V18 i0116-i0117, the V15 station timing corrected so no before-cutoff Tōji pull is asserted (PG-SA2-F0013), V13 i0147-i0153 assigned to Jigorō rather than Tōji, the earlier older-man rescue assigned to Kairi, and the dossier's report of three contradictory G4 narrative cases. These are documented within two same-authored artifacts and are not independently audited, so B is not supported.

Character-known is defined as explicitly received, directly observed or securely recalled at the cutoff, and reader-known is never automatically character-known; a missing cutoff is an abstention condition. States carry frontier limits, and vectors target leakage directly (T-VEC-03 at V02 i0062, T-VEC-04 at V03 i0174, T-VEC-08 at V17 i0162 flagging V18 as unavailable, T-VEC-09 pairing V18 i0115 with i0132). A is not supported: no default state, multi-volume spans, no in-world dates and unexecuted vectors.

scenario_readiness.note: The evidence analyzes a handful of situated written forms and abstains from unsupported exact wording; it gives no conversational model or acoustic delivery. Lines written for Tōji beyond the analyzed forms would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Tōji's actual speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Any named dossier state T01-T12 or V01-V18 cutoff; no state after V18 i0146.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Any counterpart, including Momo, Kairi, Sae and Misao as the evidence describes them at the named cutoff; the refusal does not depend on the partner.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts outside the canon cutoffs
Adult career, finance, parenting, family-conflict or clinical-risk situations
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than retrieval of a canon state

scenario_readiness.note: The dossier's overlay states there is no reliable adult career, finance, parenting or family-conflict reconstruction and no clinical risk algorithm, and T-VEC-10 requires abstention on future accountability and family life. Its states are retrieval cards for canon cutoffs, not a basis for a materially novel context.

A located ordinary baseline exists in dating, school and shop work, but it is bounded to those episodes and the coverage note says family and adult life are thin or absent; no procedure for an unfamiliar ordinary scene is given. Bounded canon questions about the located episodes remain answerable.

His stated decision frames are located, but the evidence shows them breached under threatened loss and abstains on later accountability. No procedure for a new ethical choice by Tōji can be run on this evidence set.

conditions: A dossier state T01-T12 or an equally exact V01-V18 cutoff is named; no default state is assumed and no information after the cutoff or unreceived by Tōji is used.
The partner is Momo Adachi as the evidence describes her at that cutoff; her captions are not his knowledge and her gratitude is not obligation.
Output is a description of Tōji's accessible knowledge, avowed and inferred priorities and actual conduct, with the dossier's abstentions kept; no quoted dialogue is produced as canon.

Both the honored stops (V04 reflex stop, V16, V18 i0115, i0133) and the V18 i0123-i0132 restraint are represented; no blanket patience or control rule is applied, and earlier assent never authorizes later contact.
No outcome after V18 i0146, later apology, accountability or future contact is asserted.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence set is centred on the Momo romance and supplies, for each named state, what Tōji knows, his avowed and inferred priorities and his ordered actions. Readiness is conditional because the supported use is retrieval and bounded description at a canon cutoff, not prediction of a new romantic outcome; the vectors are unexecuted and operational acceptance is blocked.

His work is V14-V15 shop labor and scheduling plus school performance and research, and the dossier states no reliable adult career reconstruction is possible. No workplace behavior beyond the located episodes can be supported.

known_limits.statement: The dossier states it does not implement the G4 runner, alter its rules, rerun its cases or claim operational acceptance; its records are retrospective evidence organizations, not personality scores or policies, and the monograph claims no operational reconstruction.

The ten T-VEC vectors are proposed, unexecuted and not held out; the dossier reports the existing G4 prototype's three contradictory narrative cases and supplies no new accuracy estimate, and operational acceptance is BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION.

No global 'respects stops' or 'always controls' rule fits: honored stops (V04, V16, V18 i0115, i0133) and the V18 i0123-i0132 door block, wrist pinning and escalation without depicted assent must both be represented, and the later release does not erase the restraint.
Reader-known is not character-known: Momo's captions, Sae's authorship of the farewell message, Kairi's emergency and later disclosures cannot be installed in an earlier state of Tōji's knowledge.
No completed intercourse is established in V05-V06, at the V15 inn (agreement to do nothing until morning, V18 i0116-i0117) or in the V18 hotel; Sae's boasts are not evidence of sexual acts.
Family conflict, adult career, finance, parenting and post-ending recovery are thin or absent; no clinical risk algorithm or long-term reliability may be supplied.

Both artifacts carry SECOND_PASS_SCOPED_SEMANTIC_REVIEW_PASSED_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING, were authored and accepted within the project's own second pass, and are active_provisional; the dossier's compiler directly read only V15-V18.

The volume readings, four ledgers, source receipts, second-pass audit and reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments and the G4 rules, cases and results are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants and the project's preserved probe failures were not rechecked here. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
